markers.mechanism: Direct translation of Spanish tener X años (to have X years) instead of English 'to be X years old'.
markers.prompt_hint: Convert 'I have N years' patterns to 'I am N years old' when describing age.

markers.mechanism: Direct translation of Spanish hacer una pregunta (to make a question).
markers.prompt_hint: Replace 'make a question' with 'ask a question'.

markers.mechanism: Spanish is pro-drop; learners omit dummy 'it' and referential subjects in non-pro-drop English.
markers.prompt_hint: Insert dummy or referential subjects ('it', 'there', 'I', 'we', 'they') where English requires an overt subject.

markers.mechanism: Spanish uses definite articles for generic and abstract nouns; learners over-apply 'the' in English.
markers.prompt_hint: Drop 'the' before generic, abstract, or plural-generic nouns (society, freedom, life, people, women, etc.) when used in a generic sense.

markers.mechanism: Spanish allows post-verbal subjects with unaccusative verbs (arrive, exist, appear); English requires SV order.
markers.prompt_hint: Restore Subject-Verb order when an unaccusative verb (arrive, exist, appear, come, happen) precedes its subject.

markers.mechanism: Spanish en covers English in/on/at; learners default to 'in' for all spatial prepositions.
markers.prompt_hint: Correct 'in' to 'on' (vehicles, surfaces, days) or 'at' (specific locations, times) where English distinguishes.

markers.mechanism: Spanish a marks both endpoint ('to the boat') and direction ('toward the boat'); English distinguishes them.
markers.prompt_hint: When the speaker means direction (not arrival) with manner-of-motion verbs (swim, run, walk, drive), use 'toward' instead of 'to'.

markers.mechanism: Spanish places attributive adjectives after the noun by default; English places them before.
markers.prompt_hint: Move post-nominal attributive adjectives to pre-nominal position (the car red → the red car).

markers.mechanism: Spanish requires negative concord (No veo nada = literally 'I don't see nothing'); English does not.
markers.prompt_hint: When two negatives appear in one clause, replace the second with its any-series equivalent (nothing→anything, nobody→anybody, never→ever, no→any).

markers.mechanism: Spanish uses definite articles ('the hands', 'the head') for body parts and clothing where English uses possessives.
markers.prompt_hint: Replace definite articles with possessive determiners (my, your, his, her, our, their) before body parts and personal clothing.

notes: Spanish typology: pro-drop, flexible word order with unaccusative inversion, definite articles for generics, single spatial preposition 'en'. Patterns broadly apply to other Iberian Romance languages with caveats.
